title: Impact of Surprise Tariff Announcements on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using a market model to compute abnormal returns, then aggregating to cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) over the immediate post-announcement window.
- Why: Surprise tariff announcements are discrete, well-timed information shocks. An event study isolates the immediate valuation impact on exposed firms by comparing realized returns to “normal” expected returns based on the market model.
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding events in the short event window (e.g., [0,1]) that systematically affect these stocks.
  - The market model is correctly specified so that abnormal returns (AR = ret − beta × mkt_ret) capture news about tariffs. We assume alpha ≈ 0 in the baseline; as robustness we estimate firm-specific alphas/betas using pre-event data.
  - No leakage or anticipation (pre-trends absent); validated via placebo pre-event window.
  - Cross-sectional inference: average CAR across stocks is informative; short-window reduces concerns about time-varying risk premia.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(broom)
  library(purrr)
})

#---------------------------
# 1) Read data
#---------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s66_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

#---------------------------
# 2) Baseline abnormal returns using provided beta (alpha = 0)
#    AR_it = ret_it - beta_i * mkt_ret_it
#---------------------------
df_base <- df %>%
  mutate(ar_base = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# Helper: summarize CAR over a given window vector (inclusive)
car_summary <- function(data, ar_col, window_vec, label){
  stock_car <- data %>%
    filter(event_day %in% window_vec) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(car = sum(.data[[ar_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  N <- nrow(stock_car)
  mu <- mean(stock_car$car)
  sdv <- sd(stock_car$car)
  se <- sdv / sqrt(N)
  tval <- ifelse(se > 0, mu / se, NA_real_)
  pval <- ifelse(is.finite(tval), 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = N - 1), NA_real_)
  ci_lo <- mu + qt(0.025, df = N - 1) * se
  ci_hi <- mu + qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se
  
  list(
    label = label,
    N = N,
    mean_CAR = mu,
    sd = sdv,
    se = se,
    t = tval,
    p = pval,
    ci_lo = ci_lo,
    ci_hi = ci_hi,
    stock_car = stock_car
  )
}

# Define windows
w_0_1 <- 0:1
w_0_0 <- 0:0
w_0_2 <- 0:2
w_placebo <- -2:-1

# Baseline summaries
res_base_01 <- car_summary(df_base, "ar_base", w_0_1, "Baseline CAR[0,1]")
res_base_00 <- car_summary(df_base, "ar_base", w_0_0, "Baseline CAR[0,0]")
res_base_02 <- car_summary(df_base, "ar_base", w_0_2, "Baseline CAR[0,2]")
res_base_pl <- car_summary(df_base, "ar_base", w_placebo, "Placebo CAR[-2,-1]")

# Also report Average Abnormal Return (AAR) on day 0
aar_day0 <- df_base %>%
  filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(ar0 = sum(ar_base), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    mean_AAR0 = mean(ar0),
    sd = sd(ar0),
    se = sd / sqrt(N),
    t = ifelse(se > 0, mean_AAR0 / se, NA_real_),
    p = ifelse(is.finite(t), 2 * pt(-abs(t), df = N - 1), NA_real_),
    ci_lo = mean_AAR0 + qt(0.025, df = N - 1) * se,
    ci_hi = mean_AAR0 + qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se
  )

#---------------------------
# 3) Robustness A: Estimate firm-specific alpha and beta using pre-event data
#    Estimation window: event_day in [-10, -2] (exclude -1 to avoid leak)
#---------------------------
est_window <- -10:-2
df_est <- df %>% filter(event_day %in% est_window)

# Fit ret ~ 1 + mkt_ret by stock if enough points; else fallback to provided beta and alpha=0
coefs <- df_est %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    if(nrow(.x) >= 5){
      fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .x)
      tibble(alpha_hat = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]], beta_hat = coef(fit)[["mkt_ret"]])
    } else {
      tibble(alpha_hat = 0, beta_hat = unique(.x$beta)[1])
    }
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

df_ols <- df %>%
  left_join(coefs, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_hat = ifelse(is.na(alpha_hat), 0, alpha_hat),
    beta_hat  = ifelse(is.na(beta_hat), beta, beta_hat),
    ar_ols = ret - alpha_hat - beta_hat * mkt_ret
  )

res_ols_01 <- car_summary(df_ols, "ar_ols", w_0_1, "OLS-Adj CAR[0,1]")
res_ols_00 <- car_summary(df_ols, "ar_ols", w_0_0, "OLS-Adj CAR[0,0]")
res_ols_02 <- car_summary(df_ols, "ar_ols", w_0_2, "OLS-Adj CAR[0,2]")
res_ols_pl <- car_summary(df_ols, "ar_ols", w_placebo, "OLS Placebo CAR[-2,-1]")

#---------------------------
# 4) Robustness B: Winsorize CAR at 1%/99% (baseline AR)
#---------------------------
winsorize <- function(x, probs = c(0.01, 0.99)){
  qq <- quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE, type = 7)
  pmin(pmax(x, qq[1]), qq[2])
}

wins_summary <- function(stock_car_df, label){
  stock_car_df <- stock_car_df %>% mutate(car_w = winsorize(car))
  N <- nrow(stock_car_df)
  mu <- mean(stock_car_df$car_w)
  sdv <- sd(stock_car_df$car_w)
  se <- sdv / sqrt(N)
  tval <- ifelse(se > 0, mu / se, NA_real_)
  pval <- ifelse(is.finite(tval), 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = N - 1), NA_real_)
  ci_lo <- mu + qt(0.025, df = N - 1) * se
  ci_hi <- mu + qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se
  list(label = label, N = N, mean_CAR = mu, sd = sdv, se = se, t = tval, p = pval, ci_lo = ci_lo, ci_hi = ci_hi)
}

res_wins_01 <- wins_summary(res_base_01$stock_car, "Winsorized CAR[0,1] (baseline AR)")

#---------------------------
# 5) Print results
#---------------------------
print_result <- function(res){
  cat(sprintf("%s: N=%d, Mean CAR=%.4f, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              res$label, res$N, res$mean_CAR, res$t, res$p, res$ci_lo, res$ci_hi))
}

cat("Primary results (equal-weighted across stocks):\n")
print_result(res_base_01)
print_result(res_base_00)
print_result(res_base_02)

cat("\nPlacebo (pre-event):\n")
print_result(res_base_pl)

cat("\nAverage Abnormal Return on day 0 (AAR0):\n")
with(aar_day0, cat(sprintf("AAR0: N=%d, Mean=%.4f, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
                           N, mean_AAR0, t, p, ci_lo, ci_hi)))

cat("\nRobustness A: Using estimated alpha and beta from pre-event window [-10,-2]\n")
print_result(res_ols_01)
print_result(res_ols_00)
print_result(res_ols_02)
print_result(res_ols_pl)

cat("\nRobustness B: Winsorized CAR at 1%/99% (Baseline AR)\n")
print_result(res_wins_01)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Surprise tariff announcements should reduce expected cash flows for internationally exposed firms and/or raise uncertainty, producing negative abnormal returns on announcement.
- Magnitude: For a 2-day window [0,1], a CAAR around −1% to −2% is plausible; day 0 AAR around −0.7% to −1.5%. The exact magnitude depends on exposure intensity and the surprise component, but we expect statistically significant negatives in [0,0] and [0,1], near zero in the placebo window.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Leverage the event-day variation around the surprise announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The surprise tariff announcement led to a significant decrease in CAR for exposed industries.
